memo.verdict: Park. Bullish on the business, neutral on the shares at CHF 264.60; conviction medium. The park rule does not force it (management B, business quality B, predictability B, trackability A, no gate tripped); the park is a price judgement. Sonova is a self-help case on top of a product cycle in a quality oligopoly leader, compelling as a business and not compelling as an investment at this price: the shares re-rated from about 16x to 20.2x two-year-forward earnings between May and October 2026, so the price pays in advance for a crowded H2 2026 launch window that has not been won, and the modal return from CHF 264.60 is 8.5 percent a year over eighteen months and 9.4 percent a year over three, against the 20 percent bar. Two re-entry triggers: the price below about CHF 227, where the modal path clears the bar over eighteen months (below CHF 200 on both horizons); or the September to November 2026 VA data and the 12-Nov-2026 H1 FY2027 print confirming the launch window won (total VA unit share at or above 50 percent, wholesale growth at or above 7 percent in local currency), at which point the bull branch's odds rise and the return is re-run at the price then prevailing.
case: - The change inside the company is real, broad and acted on. A complete change of leadership between June and December 2025 chose to narrow the perimeter (Consumer Hearing, about 5 percent of revenue at a CHF 35.8m normalised EBITA loss, into discontinued operations; a permanent 200 basis point margin gain), regionalise (four regions live 1-Apr-2026), take cost out (CHF 90m run-rate by year four) and set a growth algorithm (5 to 10 percent local-currency sales, 7 to 12 percent core EBIT, CHF 6bn by FY2030/31), and did all four within a year. The screen's rule is met twice: a chief-executive change together with a guidance-framework increase, five of twelve internal forces strong, none of the seven red flags present; the one to watch is empire-building, because CHF 6bn needs CHF 700 to 800m of unannounced acquisitions.

- The external forces net to neutral, and the two headwinds are the two that bind the return. Competition D: Zeal took 18 to 24 percent of the VA custom category within a month of its May 2026 entry and cut Sonova's combined rechargeable and multi-processor custom share from 61 to 45 percent by June 2026; four of five majors launch premium platforms in H2 2026 (Reveal and Sensia announced August 2026; Demant raised guidance on Reveal on 9-Oct-2026); Amplifon's GN Hearing purchase phases out about CHF 60m. Against that, total VA unit share rose to 54.0 percent in July 2026, +450 basis points year on year, and wholesale prices stayed stable. The franc D: translation cut FY2026 sales by CHF 221.0m and normalised EBITA by CHF 106.5m; the cost base is about 15 percent in francs against 1 percent of sales; hedges run one to six months (CHF 277.7m of forwards at March 2026); the environment is a European credit-and-sovereign stress episode in which the franc is bought. Demand C (market 2 to 4 percent, VA purchases +8 percent in June and +13 percent in July 2026, French renewal wave +6 to +8 percent); disruption B (over-the-counter disproved: Sony and Lucid withdrew, 4 percent adoption, returns near 30 percent; DEEPSONIC runs 7.7 billion neural operations a second with a two-to-three-year lead that is temporary); supply B (gross margin held at 73.7 percent through the Mexicali ramp and a dual-chip bill of materials about 10 percent dearer, covered by the 10 percent Sphere premium); own cycle B (mid-cycle; the Costco, VA and Virto R tailwinds annualise in H2 FY2027).

- The outputs so far are the product cycle's, not the corporate change's. Infinio and Sphere launched in August 2024 under the previous team; wholesale +10.9 percent local currency in H2 FY2026 against a 2 to 4 percent market; Virto R at about CHF 120m run-rate, over 60 percent of the VA rechargeable custom category. Year-two savings, the exit's accretion in the continuing accounts, the regional model's commercial effect and the Asian build are forecasts. This is why 'Major Corporate Change' is crisp on inputs and less crisp on maturity (C).
counter_case: - At the whole-case level, the "false friend": the growth is real and the earnings are deceptive, the first derivative good and the second already turning. Retail store growth in Germany and Canada (CHF 80 to 100m a year of bolt-ons with no published hurdle) masks margin dilution from lead-generation costs the market cannot see; Costco volumes at $300 to $400 and managed care at $300 to $500 lift units while the group average price decays; the Costco re-entry, the VA contract gains and Virto R all annualise in H2 FY2027 at the moment Demant's Reveal, GN's Sensia and WS Audiology's platform launch into the same channels; Zeal has already cut Sonova's custom share in the VA from 61 to 45 percent; Amplifon phases out about CHF 60m from late FY2027; the franc takes 2 to 3 points a year off core EBIT; at 20x with the consensus target below the price the downside is Morgan Stanley's CHF 135 at 14x on CHF 9.62 or Jefferies' CHF 128; the research's own analysis of competing hypotheses scored this profile with zero hard inconsistencies against four for the bull case and a 65 percent joint probability of compounding channel and competitive failure. The record concedes the annualisation (arithmetic), the custom-category loss (in the VA data), the Amplifon phase-out (the buyer's stated plan), the franc (structural until the cost base moves), and the opacity of retail unit economics (the chief executive declines to discuss Costco or margin by customer). The record holds that this is a hypothesis about the second derivative of a business whose first derivative is good on every public series (total VA share +450 basis points year on year to 54.0 percent after Zeal's entry; wholesale +10.9 percent against a 2 to 4 percent market; gross margin held at 73.7 percent; leverage 1.1x; a permanent 200 basis point gain from the exit), that it has two dated public tests (two consecutive months of total VA share below 48 percent; an H1 FY2027 wholesale print below 5.0 percent local currency), and that a zero-inconsistency score is a property of a hypothesis predicting a deterioration that has not yet appeared, not evidence that it will. Where the counter-case and the record agree: at CHF 264.60 the modal return does not clear the bar, so the "false friend" need not be true for the shares to be the wrong price; it need only be possible.

- At 'Foundations': the moat is a two-year head start; leads are caught up within one to two cycles (Bernstein's own view); Demant's custom entry took 13 points of value share in a quarter; Oticon Intent is sleeker than Sphere; private practices complain of nickel-and-dime support and repair delays; the franchise is a sequence of product bets and this window is crowded. Conceded: the silicon lead is a cadence asset and the custom loss shows how fast a gap is punished. Held at B because the non-rotating parts of the moat kept total share rising through the quarter in which the custom category was lost, and the financial outputs give the company the resources to keep re-earning the lead.
triggers: - Whether the smaller Sphere form factor (planned August 2026 for the November VA procurement window) has launched: not confirmed in any source; treated as pending.

- The launch window: Alarm level total VA unit share below 50 percent for a month; Invalidate level two consecutive months below 48 percent; custom rechargeable share Alarm below 45 percent for a month; wholesale local-currency growth Alarm below 7 percent, Invalidate an H1 FY2027 print below 5.0 percent (12-Nov-2026). A win (total share at or above 50 percent, wholesale at or above 7 percent) raises the bull branch's odds and re-runs the return at the price then prevailing.

- Margin drop-through: a core EBIT margin above 24 percent in FY2027 (reported May 2027) would move the view up; a gross margin below 73 percent for a half-year, or core EBIT margin below 22.0 percent in FY2027, down.

- The franc: EUR/CHF back above the 0.95 average of FY2025 would change the view; a 5 percent appreciation of either pair against the guidance rate is the Alarm level; a 10 percent move in a quarter is about CHF 100m of reported EBITA.
- Price: re-entry below about CHF 227 (eighteen-month horizon) or about CHF 200 (both horizons) on the modal path.

- Capital allocation: a published return hurdle or a disclosed post-acquisition return; a deal above CHF 300m without a hurdle is the Alarm level; CHF 6bn needs CHF 700 to 800m of unannounced acquisitions.
